applied.name: Buck Creek Trail / Chiwawa River Trail fork
Beverly Creek Trail (FST 1391) / Fourth Creek Trail (FST 1226.1) junction
Fourth Creek / Ingalls Creek confluence camp
East-shore gully to the Jabberwocky notch

waypoints.name: Trinity Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of Chiwawa River Road FR 6200; self-issue wilderness permit and a Northwest Forest Pass or $5/day recreation pass required at the kiosk; vault toilet, no potable water.
waypoints.directions: Drive Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to its end at the old Trinity mine site. The road is rough and high clearance is worth having; it commonly stays snowbound until early summer, which sets the start of the season here more than conditions on the peak do. Carry water from home — there is none at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Buck Creek Trail / Chiwawa River Trail fork
waypoints.note: Bear right off Buck Creek Trail #1513 onto Chiwawa River Trail #1550, which follows an old mining-road grade up the valley.
waypoints.directions: Start up-valley on Buck Creek Trail #1513 for about a mile and a half. Bear right at the fork; #1550 takes over an old mining-road grade and stays close to the river, so water is reliable along this whole stretch.

waypoints.name: Red Mountain Trail junction
waypoints.note: Stay on Chiwawa River Trail #1550 toward Chiwawa Basin; the other fork climbs to Red Mountain and Buck Creek Pass instead.
waypoints.directions: A couple more easy miles on the old road bed beside the river. This is the last water that is both obvious and easy to reach before the basin, so fill here — the tread beyond the junction gets rougher and braids in places.

waypoints.name: Chiwawa River ford
waypoints.note: Cold, knee-deep ford of the Chiwawa River (crossed once in, once out); tread gets brushy and faint beyond this point.
waypoints.directions: Past the junction the trail deteriorates and climbs through forest toward the basin. The crossing is unbridged and there is no way around it; it is manageable at typical summer flow but higher and pushier early in the season, so take the time to pick a line rather than accepting the first one. Note the spot, since you cross it again on the way out.

waypoints.name: Leave trail in upper Chiwawa Basin
waypoints.note: Maintained tread peters out in the basin's upper meadows; begin cross-country travel toward the 6,300 ft camp benches, following sporadic flagging.
waypoints.directions: Above the ford the brush thickens and the tread fades and braids. Favour the more open, less-timbered ground along the east side of the basin — drifting into the timber turns this into a bushwhack. Watch for a faint branch near the meadow edge that is easy to walk straight past; if you miss it, aim for the obvious basin above and pick your way up through the generally open forest.

waypoints.name: Chiwawa Basin high camp benches
waypoints.note: Small dirt benches with just enough flat ground for two tents; water from small trickling streams nearby; the standard overnight base for the col.
waypoints.directions: Several lines reach the bench from the basin. The left-trending gully is the most direct and the easiest going, though it is wet; the vegetated slopes beside the talus gullies are the alternative and are the better choice coming down. Early season these are snow gullies, faster than the loose summer scree but worth an ice axe.

waypoints.name: Fortress-Chiwawa col (notch on Fortress's east ridge)
waypoints.note: Moderate snow slope steepens noticeably near the notch (ice axe recommended); rock off to the sides is loose and sandy.
waypoints.directions: From the bench traverse steep heather and aim for the notch in Fortress's east ridge. The snow slope leading up to it is moderate but steepens noticeably in the last stretch below the notch, and the rock flanking it is loose and sandy — stay on the snow or the most solid line you can find rather than escaping onto the sides.

waypoints.name: Chiwawa Mountain summit
waypoints.note: Two summit rocks about 30 ft apart with little to distinguish which is the true high point; views of Glacier Peak and Fortress Mountain.
waypoints.directions: From the col work up the southwest side on slabs, gullies and talus, taking the path of least resistance rather than any single line. The crux is the short step gaining the summit ridge — loose, exposed Class 2-3 — after which an easy traverse of about 100 ft to the west/right reaches the top. Picking the wrong gully near the col is the standard mistake here and leads to an exposed low-fifth-class dead end, so back off and re-read the terrain rather than forcing it.

waypoints.name: Beverly Turnpike Trailhead
waypoints.note: Shared trailhead with Bean Creek Basin at the end of the rough, overgrown FR 9737-112 spur road.
waypoints.directions: From the North Fork Teanaway River Road, turn onto the FR-9737-112 spur and follow it to its end at the Beverly Turnpike trailhead, around 3,650 ft. The spur is rough and overgrown, and the gravel access opens with spring snowmelt; that plus the Ingalls Creek ford further along makes July through September the practical window. It is the shared lot with Bean Creek Basin, so at about half a mile bear left onto signed Trail #1391 rather than taking the Bean Creek fork, which is a commonly reported mistake here.

waypoints.name: Beverly Creek Trail (FST 1391) / Fourth Creek Trail (FST 1226.1) junction
waypoints.note: Faint fork in forested/open terrain; bear toward Fourth Creek Trail for the pass rather than continuing up Beverly Creek.

waypoints.name: Fourth Creek Pass
waypoints.note: Low, treed pass on the drainage divide reached via a steep final 0.3-mile push; descends into the Fourth Creek drainage on the far side.

waypoints.name: Fourth Creek / Ingalls Creek confluence camp
waypoints.note: Established basecamp near the creek confluence used by most south-side parties before the summit push.

waypoints.name: Ingalls Creek ford
waypoints.note: Potentially dangerous ford — cold and swift in early season, can be partially frozen with slick ice-covered rocks.

waypoints.name: South-side gully, west of the main gully
waypoints.note: Class 2 scrambling up loose rock in the gully just west of Argonaut's main south gully, heading for the summit ridge.

waypoints.name: Argonaut Peak summit (west summit, true)
waypoints.note: Final moves onto the true (west) summit ridge are harder than the class 2 approach suggests, often low class 3/4.

waypoints.name: Trinity Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of Chiwawa River Road/FR-6200 (last 12 mi rough gravel); pay day-use fee or NW Forest Pass and self-issue a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit at the kiosk.

waypoints.name: Chiwawa River footbridge
waypoints.note: Plank/log bridge crossing the Chiwawa River about three miles up the trail — solid underfoot despite an ominous warning sign posted at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Buck Creek Pass
waypoints.note: Established camps in scattered trees and meadows; most parties base camp here for the climb, with a junction to the Flower Dome Trail #799 a half mile north.

waypoints.name: Basin below Buck's south/southwest slopes
waypoints.note: Leave the maintained trail at the pass and contour/ascend cross-country into the open basin beneath the peak's south and southwest slopes — start of the actual scramble.

waypoints.name: Snowfield and loose schist below the summit
waypoints.note: A firm, sometimes icy snowfield crossing leads into loose, exfoliating Class 2-3 schist blocks just right of the obvious white scar — significant rockfall risk for parties below.

waypoints.name: Buck Mountain
waypoints.note: True summit; sweeping views of Glacier Peak, Clark Mountain, and the Napeequa valley — first climbed in 1948 by Carl Suback and Ray Rigg.

waypoints.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.note: Standard approach: Snow Lakes Trail #1553 (~4.2 mi up Icicle Creek Rd from US-2 in Leavenworth) into the Enchantment Lakes basin, then via Perfection Lake to Prusik Pass, traverse NW to the Druid Plateau, then to the summit block (roughly 13-14 mi and over 7,300 ft of gain one-way).

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Trail #1599 up Mountaineer Creek.

waypoints.name: Stuart/Colchuck Trail Split
waypoints.note: Colchuck Lake Trail breaks left from the Stuart Lake Trail.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake
waypoints.note: Popular camp/bivy at the lake outlet, below Dragontail and Colchuck Peak.

waypoints.name: East-shore gully to the Jabberwocky notch
waypoints.note: From the lake's eastern shoreline and talus, climb the obvious loose gully toward the notch above Jabberwocky Tower; the upper part is rope-up terrain, and Class 3 ground leads from the notch onto the NW Ridge.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Balanced Rock
waypoints.note: Summit via the NW Ridge.
